BIRLA INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY, MESRA, RANCHI
(MID SEMESTER EXAMINATION)

CLASS: B. TECH   SEMESTER: IV
BRANCH: PRODUCTION   SESSION : SP/2020

SUBJECT: PE209 ENGINEERING ECONOMY, COSTING AND ACCOUNTING

TIME: 2 HOURS   FULL MARKS: 25

INSTRUCTIONS:
1. The total marks of the questions are 25.
2. Candidates may attempt for all 25 marks.
3. Before attempting the question paper, be sure that you have got the correct question paper.
4. The missing data, if any, may be assumed suitably.
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    CO BL
Q1 (a) What does it mean by economic equivalence? [2] CO1 BL2
Q1 (b) A company planned Rs. 20,00,000 investment in 2012, which is a present worth
in the year 2012 of anticipated phase wise investments during the next 4 years
from 2013 to 2016. Assume the amount planned for 2013 is Rs. 10,00,000 with
constant  decrease  of  Rs.  2,50,000  each  year  thereafter.  Does  the  planned
decreasing investment series equal the announced Rs. 20,00,000 in 2012 using
time value of money worth 10%?
[3] CO1 BL4

Q2 (a) Differentiate  between  mutually  exclusive  alternatives  and  independent
projects?
[2] CO1 BL2
Q2 (b) An electronic part manufacturing company must choose one of two different
assembly  methods.  Method  A  will  cost  Rs.  80,000  to  buy  and  will  have  an
annual operating cost of Rs. 6,000 over its 4-year service life. Method B will
cost Rs. 1,30,000 initially with an annual operating cost of Rs. 4,000 over its
8-year life. Methods A will have no salvage value, but method B will have some
equipment worth an estimated Rs. 12,000. Which method should be selected
if the alternatives are exclusive? Use present worth at an interest rate of 15%
per year.
[3] CO1 BL4

Q3 (a) How do you perform replacement analysis? [2] CO2 BL3
 (b) Machine A has remaining service life of 2 years and its current market value is
Rs. 3,000. While a new automatic machine B costs Rs. 12,000 has a life of 5
years.  Operating  cost  for  machine  A  is  Rs.  4,000  per  year,  while  that  of
machine B is Rs. 2,000 only. Perform a replacement study by cconsidering 15%
interest rate.
[3] CO2 BL4

Q4 (a) Explain sinking fund method of calculating depreciation. [2] CO2 BL2
 (b) The purchase cost of an equipment is Rs. 40,000. It has useful life of 5 years.
The salvage value at the end of useful life is Rs. 2,000. Calculate the annual
depreciation and book value of the equipment at the end of 4th  year using
sum-of-years-digits method.
[3] CO2 BL3

Q5 (a) Differentiate between explicit cost and implicit cost. [2] CO4 BL2
Q5 (b) Explain with example: Sunk cost, Out-of-pocket cost, and Opportunity cost. [3] CO4 BL2

[Data for Q2 & Q3]       Discrete Cash Flow: Compound Interest Factors (at interest rate 15%)
